newsitem.title: EGYPT: Heavy rains wash away houses, trees in south Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Heavy rains wash away houses, trees in south Egypt.

text.p: Heavy rains lashed southern Egypt, uprooting trees and washing away houses, but there were no reports of casualties, Egyptian newspapers said on Thursday.

They said the rains, which lasted for up to 10 hours on Wednesday, washed away at least 30 houses in the southern tourist resort of Aswan and in Sohag province. The rains also felled telephone and electricity poles, the papers added.
Pumps removed water that gathered at the ancient Temple of Horus in Edfu town but antiquities inspectors said the water did not damage any of Aswan's other antiquities.
Train services between the capital Cairo and Aswan were disrupted after rain water covered the tracks, the papers said.
In 1994, about 80 people were killed and hundreds of houses washed away after heavy rain flooded villages in Sohag and the tourist resort of Luxor.
